people.name: Mrs. Kostyra
people.role: Martha's mother Martha Kostyra (née Ruszkowski, born 1914 Buffalo, died Nov 15 2007 Norwalk CT) — known as "Big Martha". Polish-American matriarch of the Kostyra clan. Featured on dozens of MSL TV cooking segments demonstrating Polish family recipes — pierogi, sauerbraten, chrusciki (bow-tie cookies), babka, kielbasa, lardy cake, stuffed cabbage, blueberry buckle. Martha dedicated her cookbooks Martha Stewart's Quick Cook (1983) and Martha Stewart's Pies & Tarts (1985) to her.

people.name: Marc Morrone
people.role: Pet expert (born June 1 1960, the Bronx). Co-founded Parrots of the World pet shop in Rockville Centre, NY with Nick Guerra in 1978. Joined Martha Stewart Living TV in 1997 as resident pet expert; ran "Ask Marc", Bird Breed, Reptile Breed, Pocket Breed, Exotic Breed, Dog Breed segments. MSLO gave him his own spin-off Petkeeping with Marc Morrone (2003–2006). On-camera co-stars included Darwin (grey parrot), Harry (scarlet macaw), Coral Ann (cockatoo), Harvey (Flemish Giant rabbit), Splash (ferret), Emily (Burmese python). Memoir A Man for All Species (2010, foreword by Martha).

people.name: Salli LaGrone
people.role: Southern caterer and longtime friend of Martha's from their pre-TV catering days. Born Salli Shropshire May 11 1948 in Rome GA; died July 29 2011 in Franklin TN. Recurring guest on MSL TV from Season 1 — their first joint segment was a Southern fried chicken cook-off, a format Martha later recreated with Snoop Dogg. Other MSL recipes: Oyster Pie, Mushroom Pâté, Cranberry Tartlets.

people.name: Hannah Milman
people.role: Senior Vice President and Executive Editorial Director of Crafts at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia. RISD graduate; joined the magazine at its second issue (1991) and stayed two decades. Set MSL's signature craft aesthetic — wreaths, ornaments, egg-decorating, decoupage, natural-materials décor. Co-authored Great American Wreaths: The Best of Martha Stewart Living (Clarkson Potter, 1996) with Martha and Gael Towey. On-camera segments include "Sunflower Wreath with Hannah".

people.name: Gael Towey
people.role: Founding Art Director of Martha Stewart Living magazine; longtime second-in-command on the creative side. "Origami with Gail" segment (MSL S7 E212V) — "Gael" is pronounced "Gail".

people.name: Kit Anderson
people.role: Gardening expert and longtime contributor; led shopping-for-plants and perennials segments.

people.name: Eric Ripert
people.role: Chef and owner of Le Bernardin (NYC); recurring Master Chefs collaborator on seafood.

people.name: Rick Bayless
people.role: Chef and Mexican-cuisine expert; Frontera Grill, Chicago. Master Chefs collaborator.

people.name: Diana Kennedy
people.role: Mexican-cuisine cookbook author; appeared as Master Chefs guest.

people.name: Anne Willan
people.role: Founder of La Varenne cooking school; French-cuisine cookbook author. Master Chefs guest.

people.name: Jonathan Adler
people.role: Potter and designer; visited for pottery demonstration (Jonathan Adler Pottery segment, Season 7).

people.name: Todd English
people.role: Chef and restaurateur (Olives, Figs); appeared in Master Chefs segments demonstrating pizza dough and Italian techniques.

people.name: Lord Wedgwood
people.role: Lord Piers Wedgwood, 4th Baron Wedgwood — descendant of Josiah Wedgwood; appeared discussing the Wedgwood ceramics tradition.

people.name: David Dawn
people.role: Garden featured in MSL TV — David Dawn's Garden, Hudson Valley.

people.name: Michael Romano
people.role: Executive chef of Union Square Cafe (NYC) from 1988; co-author with Danny Meyer of The Union Square Cafe Cookbook (1994). Featured in MSL TV "Caesar Salad with Michael", "Spinach Cannelloni with Michael", and "Interview with Michael" segments (e.g. MSL Season 6 Ep. 126V).

people.name: Josefina Howard
people.role: Founder of Rosa Mexicano (NYC, 1984). Born in Cuba, trained as a designer. Appeared on MSL TV January 1998 making avocado-orange-tequila soup with Martha; her quesadilla segment is also documented. Book: Rosa Mexicano: A Culinary Autobiography.

people.name: Franck Deletrain
people.role: French chef in NYC (Brasserie 8½, Patroon, Café Centro). From Martha's Kitchen episode "Franck Deletrain" (2001). "Steak with Franck" segments.

people.name: Koichi Hara
people.role: Sake-tasting segment guest.

people.name: Chris (Storing Linens)
people.role: Recurring on storing-linens segments ("Storing Linens with Chris").

people.name: Leon (Standing Rib Roast)
people.role: Recurring co-host of multi-part Standing Rib Roast segments.

people.name: Gail (Origami)
people.role: Origami demonstrations ("Origami with Gail").

people.name: Sean (Succulent Sphere)
people.role: Succulent-sphere garden craft segments.

people.name: Frances Palmer
people.role: Frances Palmer Pottery (Weston, Connecticut) — celebrated ceramist known for hand-thrown earthenware, tulipieres, and dahlia vases. Longtime Martha collaborator.

people.name: Guy Wolff
people.role: Guy Wolff Pottery (Bantam, CT) — hand-thrown English-style flower pots. Featured making garden pots and delivering them to Turkey Hill.

people.name: Linda Greenlaw
people.role: Author of The Lobster Chronicles; swordboat captain featured in Sebastian Junger's The Perfect Storm. Featured in Martha's Favorite Books segment.

people.name: Diane Wallace
people.role: Gardener featured in MSL TV (Diane Wallace's Garden field trip).

people.name: Margaret Roach
people.role: Gardening editor at Martha Stewart Living magazine; later author of A Way to Garden. Featured on MSL TV with her own garden.

people.name: Sydney Eddison
people.role: Gardener and author (Connecticut); her Newtown CT garden was a multi-part MSL TV field trip.

people.name: Thomas Hobbs
people.role: Canadian gardener and author (Shocking Beauty); Southlands Nursery, Vancouver BC. His garden featured in multi-part field trip.

people.name: Eric Pike
people.role: Creative Director at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia from the magazine's founding era; longtime visual architect of MSL's aesthetic.

people.name: Granny Foster
people.role: Featured baker on MSL TV — Granny Foster's Refrigerator Rolls (Part 1 and 2).

people.name: Kristin St. Clair
people.role: Crafter featured on MSL TV — glittered pinecone clusters and other holiday crafts.

people.name: Riad Nasr
people.role: Co-chef at Balthazar (NYC) and now chef-owner of Frenchette (NYC) with Lee Hanson. Earlier worked at Daniel under Boulud. MSL S5 E146V "Balthazar Restaurant: Brandade de Morue, Braised Ribs". Cookbook (with Hanson): Frenchette Bistro Cooking (2024).

people.name: Patricia Wells
people.role: American food writer based in Paris and Provence. Books: Bistro Cooking, Patricia Wells at Home in Provence, The Provence Cookbook, The Food Lover's Guide to Paris. MSL S7 E024V (Pistou Soup, Basic Bread Dough, Herbes de Provence, Lavender Sachet).

people.name: Terrance Brennan
people.role: Chef-owner of Picholine (NYC, opened 1993; named after the green olive). Mediterranean/French. MSL S5 E363V featured his "Sea Bass with Rhubarb Compote" and "Picholine Olives". Book: Artisanal Cooking (2005).

people.name: Scott Peacock
people.role: Southern chef of Watershed (Decatur, GA); longtime partner and collaborator with Edna Lewis. Co-author with Lewis of The Gift of Southern Cooking (2003). Appeared on MSL TV demonstrating Southern Pan-Fried Chicken.

people.name: Madhur Jaffrey
people.role: Indian cookbook author and actress. From Martha's Kitchen episode "Indian with Madhur Jaffrey" (2001). Books: An Invitation to Indian Cooking, Madhur Jaffrey's Indian Cookery, World Vegetarian.

people.name: Egidiana Maccioni
people.role: "Egi" — consulting chef at Le Cirque and Osteria del Circo (NYC); wife of Sirio Maccioni. Tuscan home cooking. MSL S6 E044V "Meeting Egi / Polenta with Sausage Stew / Tuscan Baked Tomatoes / Ciambella Coffee Cake". The Maccioni Family Cookbook (2003) photos by Elizabeth Zeschin (who also shot Martha's Garden Book).

people.name: Cesare Casella
people.role: Tuscan-born NYC chef-owner of Beppe (2001) and Maremma. Known for his signature pocket of fresh herbs in his chef-coat breast pocket. MSL S5 E196V "Tuscan Pici Pasta; Calf's Liver with Bacon and Capers" matches his style. Books: Diary of a Tuscan Chef, True Tuscan.

people.name: Daniel Boulud
people.role: Chef-owner of Daniel (NYC) and the Dinex Group. Lyon-born, classical French training. Wikipedia credits MSL TV appearances. MSL S7 E101V "Chateaubriand" and S7 E384V "Pea Soup with Mint / Salmon with Sorrel / Potato Fritter with Truffles" and S6 E074V "Cod Cockles & Chorizo Basquaise" all match his signatures.

people.name: Hiroko Shimbo
people.role: Japanese cookbook author and consultant based in NYC; dubbed "the Martha Stewart of Japan". Books: The Japanese Kitchen (2000), The Sushi Experience (2006), Hiroko's American Kitchen (2012). Likely behind MSL S7 E212V "Cooking with Miso / Making Dashi / Perfect Rice".

people.name: Mark Strausman
people.role: Italian-American NYC chef (Campagna, Coco Pazzo). Frequent Martha guest.

people.name: Guillermo Pernot
people.role: Chef-owner of Pasión! (Philadelphia); Nuevo Latino/ceviche specialist. From Martha's Kitchen episode (2003).

people.name: Mark Russ Federman
people.role: Third-generation owner of Russ & Daughters appetizing store (Lower East Side NYC, est. 1914). "Caviar with Mark" segment. Martha endorsed his memoir Russ & Daughters: Reflections and Recipes from the House That Herring Built (2013) and recalled childhood visits.

people.name: Eli Wilner
people.role: NYC's leading antique-frame specialist; Eli Wilner & Co. has framed pieces for many of Martha's homes. Likely "Tag Sale Find with Eli" segment.

people.name: Sean Conway
people.role: Garden designer; host of Cultivating Life (PBS). Plausible match for "Succulent Sphere with Sean" and "Window Boxes with Sean" segments.

people.name: Marco Polo Stufano
people.role: Founding Director of Horticulture at Wave Hill (Bronx, NY) from its 1965 founding. Pioneer of the New American Garden style.

people.name: John Fairey
people.role: Designer and founder of Peckerwood Garden (now The John Fairey Garden) in Hempstead TX (est. 1971). Died 2020.

people.name: Ed Weiss
people.role: Beekeeper who taught Martha in her Westport catering days; appeared on MSL TV at the Turkey Hill hives.

people.name: Norm Cote
people.role: Retired Norwalk firefighter and current keeper of Martha's beehives at Turkey Hill (and other Fairfield County clients).

people.name: Jo Ubogy
people.role: Connecticut breeder of Himalayan cats; supplied Martha's six composer-named seal-point Himalayans — Mozart, Beethoven, Vivaldi, Verdi, Berlioz, and Bartók.

people.name: Isolde Motley
people.role: Founding Editor-in-Chief of Martha Stewart Living magazine (1990–1992); previously founding editor of This Old House magazine.

people.name: Susan Wyland
people.role: Editor-in-Chief of Martha Stewart Living magazine 1992–1996; went on to develop Real Simple at Time Inc.

people.name: Linda Corradina
people.role: Executive Producer of Martha Stewart Living Television.

people.name: Lauren Deen
people.role: Series Producer of Martha Stewart Living Television; three-time Daytime Emmy winner.

people.name: Carolyn Kelly Wallach
people.role: MSL TV producer (1960–2004); four-time Daytime Emmy winner — the most-decorated producer on the show. Died at age 43 in Greenwich CT during the show's final months.

people.name: Greta Anthony
people.role: First-ever culinary intern at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia; later a James Beard Award winner.

people.name: Suzanne McGrath
people.role: Executive Producer of Martha Stewart Living Television.

people.name: Marcie McGoldrick
people.role: Halloween + craft editor at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia (joined 1999). Led plaster casting, paper-bag luminaries, and many of the show's signature Halloween projects.

people.name: Nobu Matsuhisa
people.role: Japanese-Peruvian chef and founder of the Nobu and Matsuhisa restaurant empire (50+ locations globally). Appeared on MSL TV before he became a household name — MSL S9 E16 (~2002). "Nobu before Nobu."

people.name: Julia Child
people.role: Pioneering television chef (1912–2004); author of Mastering the Art of French Cooking. Guest on the 1995 Martha Stewart Christmas Special demonstrating croquembouche alongside Martha.

people.name: Jacques Pépin
people.role: Legendary French-American chef, author, and TV host; longtime friend of Martha. Founder of the International Culinary Center; PBS series with Julia Child.

people.name: Jeffrey Alford
people.role: Cookbook author (with Naomi Duguid) of Hot Sour Salty Sweet, Flatbreads & Flavors, etc. — global street-food and grain cookbooks. MSL S9 multiple appearances.

people.name: David Pasternack
people.role: Chef-owner of Esca (NYC, with Mario Batali and Joe Bastianich); known for crudo and Italian seafood. MSL S9 E78.

people.name: Michel Richard
people.role: French-American chef-pastry chef (1948–2016); founded Citrus (LA), Citronelle (DC), Central. Master Chef of Pastry. MSL S9 E79.

people.name: Michael Pollan
people.role: Food and nature writer; author of The Omnivore's Dilemma, In Defense of Food, The Botany of Desire. Featured on MSL S9 E57 cider segment, pre-fame.

people.name: Dale Chihuly
people.role: Glass artist; founder of Pilchuck Glass School. Studio glass pioneer. MSL S9 E59.

people.name: Lorraine Bracco
people.role: Actress known for The Sopranos (Dr. Melfi) and Goodfellas. MSL S9 E92.

people.name: Ismail Merchant
people.role: Film producer of Merchant Ivory Productions (1936–2005); demonstrated Indian cooking on MSL S4 E9 (multipart Indian Food segment).

people.name: Damien Hirst
people.role: British contemporary artist (YBA generation). Artworks featured on MSL S9 E48/E52.

people.name: John Pawson
people.role: British minimalist architect. MSL S9 E76.

people.name: Walter Wick
people.role: Photographer; creator/illustrator of the I Spy children's-book series with Jean Marzollo. MSL S9 E75.

people.name: Melanie Falick
people.role: Knitting and craft author (Knitting in America; Handknit Holidays; later editorial director of STC Craft / Melanie Falick Books). MSL S9 E73.

people.name: Miss Piggy
people.role: Muppet character (Jim Henson). Made gingerbread house with Martha and Ben Krupinski on the 1995 Christmas Special.

people.name: Hillary Clinton
people.role: First Lady of the United States 1993–2001; later Senator, Secretary of State, presidential nominee. Demonstrated a 50-state oak-leaf wreath at the White House on the 1995 Christmas Special.

people.name: Ben Krupinski
people.role: Hamptons-based luxury builder (1942–2018); built Martha's Lily Pond Lane renovations and many other Hamptons estates. Made gingerbread house with Martha and Miss Piggy on the 1995 Christmas Special.

people.name: Johnny Batson
people.role: Poultry judge; co-judged the Central Pennsylvania Avian Club's 21st Annual Spring Show alongside Martha on May 3–4, 1997.

people.name: Alexis Stewart
people.role: Martha Stewart's only child, born 1965, a frequent on-air presence whose namesake recipes — chocolate chip cookies, egg salad sandwich, chopped vegetable salad — appeared throughout MSL cooking segments. She later became a broadcaster in her own right, co-hosting the SiriusXM radio show 'Whatever with Alexis' and Hallmark Channel's 'Whatever, Martha!' (2008–2012) with Jennifer Koppelman Hutt, and co-authored the 2011 book 'Whateverland: Learning to Live Here.'

people.name: James David
people.role: Austin, Texas landscape architect who, with partner Gary Peese, ran the influential garden shop and boutique nursery Gardens for nearly three decades along with the design studio David/Peese Design. Their steeply terraced, plant-rich two-acre garden in Austin's Rollingwood neighborhood — developed over 36 years and a fixture of Garden Conservancy Open Days tours — was the private garden toured in MSL segments; the couple later relocated to Santa Fe, New Mexico.

people.name: Dani Fiori
people.role: Emmy-winning set and prop stylist turned cookie artist who spent years with Martha Stewart's television operation as its resident cookie expert. She went on to found Sweet Dani B Cookie Kitchen, a couture-cookie bakery and hands-on workshop space in Asbury Park, New Jersey; on air she joined Martha to bedazzle gingerbread cookies and build forests of Christmas-tree cupcakes.

people.name: Mr. Cooper
people.role: Sandblasting craftsman who demonstrated the technique in an early MSL segment; the Season 1 rundown records him only by his honorific, and no fuller identification survives in the public record.

people.name: Jane Heller
people.role: Martha's longtime friend and private banker, who took Stewart on as a client around her 1987 Kmart deal and remained her banker — later a top private banker at Bank of America — through the building of her media empire. Her Season 5 appearance, cooking her signature unglazed Easter ham, is a favorite among fans of the show.

people.name: Allen Haskell
people.role: Allen C. Haskell (1935–2004), the celebrated New Bedford, Massachusetts nurseryman called "the king of topiary," whose six-acre nursery of rare plants and flawless myrtle and rosemary standards drew patrons from Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis to Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands. A recurring MSL gardening contributor, here demonstrating forced branches; his nursery is preserved today as the Trustees' Allen C. Haskell Public Gardens.

people.name: Mrs. DiPaola
people.role: Home cook who joined Martha in the MSL kitchen to bake her treasured fig cake in a two-part segment.

people.name: Colin Powell
people.role: Retired U.S. Army four-star general who served as National Security Advisor and as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (1989–1993) during the Gulf War, and later became the 65th U.S. Secretary of State. At the time of this two-part sit-down he chaired America's Promise, the youth-mentoring alliance he founded after the 1997 Presidents' Summit — the subject of the episode, listed as "America's Promise with Colin Powell."

people.name: Mobee Weinstein
people.role: Foreman of Gardeners for Outdoor Gardens at the New York Botanical Garden, where she trained at the School of Professional Horticulture, and a veteran gardening guest across many MSL seasons. She later wrote The Complete Book of Ferns (2019); here she leads a two-part seed-starting lesson.

people.name: Preston Bailey
people.role: Panamanian-born, New York-based event and floral designer whose studio, opened in 1980, became famous for transforming venues into lavish floral environments for celebrity weddings and galas; he went on to publish a shelf of entertaining-design books. Demonstrated one of his signature bouquets on MSL.

people.name: Anny Seavey
people.role: Stained-glass artist and proprietor of Hot Flash Anny's studio and gallery in Southwest Harbor, Maine, on Mount Desert Island, with decades spent designing, making, and restoring stained glass around the country; her children's window hangs over the main desk of the Southwest Harbor Public Library. Demonstrated her stained-glass craft in an MSL segment.

people.name: Robert Kinnaman
people.role: American folk-art and antiques dealer (d. 2005) who, with partner Brian Ramaekers, founded Kinnaman & Ramaekers in Houston in 1969, later a fixture of Bridgehampton on Long Island's East End. A longtime Winter Antiques Show exhibitor, he wrote for The Magazine Antiques and helped build several important collections of 18th- and 19th-century self-taught American art; his Americana collection was featured in an MSL segment.

people.name: Ralph Kovel
people.role: Ralph Kovel (1920–2008), half of America's best-known antiques-writing team with his wife Terry: together they published nearly 100 books beginning with 1953's Dictionary of Marks — Pottery and Porcelain, launched their annual antiques price guide in 1968, and wrote the longest-running syndicated antiques column in U.S. newspapers. The pair walked Martha through collecting fundamentals in the four-part 'Collecting with Kovels' segments.

people.name: Terry Kovel
people.role: Terry Kovel (b. 1928) of Shaker Heights, Ohio — co-author with her husband Ralph of nearly 100 antiques books, including the annual Kovels' Antiques & Collectibles Price Guide (over 4 million copies sold), and of the longest-running syndicated antiques column in America, a franchise she carried on after Ralph's death in 2008. Appeared with Ralph in MSL's four-part 'Collecting with Kovels' segments.

people.name: Rabbit Goody
people.role: Textile historian and master weaver who founded Thistle Hill Weavers in 1989 in a converted feed mill near Cherry Valley, New York. Her mill's short-run reproductions of historic fabrics have appeared in more than 70 films and television productions — from 'Road to Perdition' to HBO's 'John Adams' — and she demonstrated historic weaving techniques on MSL.

people.name: Sam Kasten
people.role: Master handweaver of custom textiles for the interior and architectural trades, based in the Berkshires — first Stockbridge, later Pittsfield, Massachusetts. Trained at Nantucket Looms, Kasten wove wide wall coverings for architects including Skidmore, Owings & Merrill and I.M. Pei, with work in the National Gallery of Art and the Neue Galerie; he demonstrated handweaving on MSL.

people.name: Nico De Swert
people.role: Belgian-born floral designer and interior stylist, trained at Antwerp's Royal Academy of Fine Art and based in New York, whose work appeared in Martha Stewart Living and O, The Oprah Magazine; he later published the book Living with Flowers (Abrams, 2004), which treats flowers as an artistic medium organized by color. He built a centerpiece on-air in an MSL segment.

people.name: Keb' Mo'
people.role: Stage name of Kevin Moore (b. 1951, Los Angeles), the singer-guitarist whose warm, Delta-rooted acoustic blues made him one of the genre's leading modern voices and a multiple Grammy winner for contemporary blues. Profiled in an MSL guest segment.

people.name: Ed Rice
people.role: Second-generation Tennessee ham curer behind Rice's Country Hams of Mt. Juliet, east of Nashville — a family smokehouse business started by Ed Rice Sr. and carried on by Ed Rice Jr., whose slow-cured hams have won dozens of Grand Champion titles at state and county fairs since 1971. He presented his dry-cured country ham in the show's Nashville field-trip episode.

people.name: Darcy Miller
people.role: Founding editor of Martha Stewart Weddings at its 1995 launch and its longtime editorial director; a celebrations expert and illustrator who went on to write Our Wedding Scrapbook and the bestselling Celebrate Everything! (2016), with a foreword by Martha. Appeared in an MSL wedding special.

people.name: Ray Bliss Rich
people.role: Artist who joined Martha for a segment on fish prints — the Japanese craft of gyotaku, in which a fresh-caught fish is inked and pressed onto paper to record its image.

people.name: Aretha Franklin
people.role: The Queen of Soul — 18-time Grammy winner and, in 1987, the first woman inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. She joined Martha on the 1999 holiday special Home for the Holidays: The Family Tree to make her ginger ale-glazed 'Queen of Soul Ham.'

people.name: Tony Bennett
people.role: Legendary American crooner (1926-2023) whose seven-decade career ran from 'I Left My Heart in San Francisco' through the MTV Unplugged revival and late-life duet albums, collecting some 20 Grammy Awards including a Lifetime Achievement Award. He sang 'White Christmas' as a special guest on the 2000 special Martha Stewart's Christmas Dream.

people.name: Cyndi Lauper
people.role: Pop icon who broke through with She's So Unusual (1983) and won the Best New Artist Grammy, later becoming the first woman to win a solo Tony for Best Original Score for Kinky Boots (2013). She sang 'Winter Wonderland' as a special guest on the 2000 special Martha Stewart's Christmas Dream.

people.name: Ana Gasteyer
people.role: Comedian, actress, and Saturday Night Live cast member (1996–2002) whose recurring SNL impression of Martha Stewart became famous in its own right; Martha played along, welcoming her as a special guest on the CBS holiday special Martha Stewart's Christmas Dream (2000) alongside Tony Bennett and Cyndi Lauper. The two reunited decades later for the 2024 Roku special Martha Stewart's Christmas Fever Dream.

people.name: Carlos Cortés
people.role: Third-generation San Antonio faux bois (trabajo rústico) artisan, heir to the concrete-sculpture tradition his great-uncle Dionicio Rodríguez brought to Texas around 1924 and passed on to his father Máximo Cortés. Best known for The Grotto (2009) on the San Antonio River Walk, he has also made faux bois furniture for Martha Stewart; MSL visited him for a field-trip segment on his craft.

people.name: Daisy Schwartzberg Toye
people.role: New York celebrity makeup artist, based out of the Rita Hazan Salon, who has been Martha's personal makeup artist — and close friend — for some two decades, and who later joined the cast of Bravo's The Real Housewives of New York City. In this segment she turns daytime makeup into a festive holiday-party look.

people.name: Anduin Havens
people.role: Theatre-trained set designer and art director who rose through Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia as supervising production designer, special-event designer, and on-air contributor, and later became creative director of video for the Martha Stewart and Emeril Lagasse brands at Marquee Brands. Here she joins Martha to whip up a creamy crudité dip for a potluck lunch at the Martha Stewart Living offices.

people.name: Jodi Levine
people.role: RISD-trained crafter who spent 19 years at Martha Stewart Living, rising from craft editor of the magazine to editorial director of Martha Stewart Kids and Martha Stewart Baby; she went on to found the kids-craft brand SuperMakeIt and to write the craft books Candy Aisle Crafts (2014) and Paper Goods Projects. Here she makes graham-cracker cottages with Martha — a whole village of them makes a Christmas centerpiece.

people.name: Colin Van Dervort
people.role: Metairie, Louisiana groom who, with fiancée Liz Wilks, won the grand prize in the 'Sandals Wedding by Martha Stewart' contest: a customized destination wedding at Sandals Emerald Bay on Great Exuma, Bahamas, planned by the Martha Stewart Weddings creative team and chronicled in the 2010 special Bayou to Bahamas.

people.name: Liz Wilks
people.role: Metairie, Louisiana bride (Elizabeth Wilks) who, with fiancé Colin Van Dervort, won a customized 'Sandals Wedding by Martha Stewart' dream wedding at Sandals Emerald Bay on Great Exuma, Bahamas; the Martha Stewart Weddings creative team planned the classic, elegant ceremony chronicled in the 2010 special Bayou to Bahamas.

people.name: Jamaica Kincaid
people.role: Antiguan-American novelist, essayist, and longtime New Yorker staff writer (Annie John, Lucy, A Small Place) who became an equally celebrated garden writer from her home in North Bennington, Vermont. She visited MSL to discuss My Garden (Book):, her 1999 collection of gardening essays.

people.name: Sal Gilbertie
people.role: Second-generation owner of Gilbertie's Herb Gardens in Westport, Connecticut (family firm founded 1922), one of the country's leading herb growers and author of several herb-gardening books. A Martha Stewart plant supplier for over 30 years, he appeared on Martha Stewart Living as its herb authority and later donated the plants for Martha's culinary herb garden exhibit at the New York Botanical Garden.

people.name: Fred Klatt
people.role: Tinsmith who appeared on Martha Stewart Living's first season, demonstrating traditional tin-smithing in a March 1994 segment logged in the show's archive simply as 'Tin man'.

people.name: Ruth Rogers
people.role: American-born chef who co-founded The River Café in Hammersmith, London with Rose Gray in 1987; the Thames-side Italian restaurant won a Michelin star in 1998 and its River Café cookbooks became modern classics. She presented River Café dishes with Gray on MSL in July 1998.

people.name: Rose Gray
people.role: British chef (1939-2010) who co-founded The River Café in Hammersmith, London with Ruth Rogers in 1987, championing seasonal Italian farmhouse cooking; co-author of the River Café cookbooks and co-presenter of the 1998 Channel 4 series 'The Italian Kitchen'. She presented River Café dishes with Rogers on MSL in July 1998.

people.name: Michael Hughes
people.role: Master craftsman and thrower at Josiah Wedgwood & Sons in Barlaston, England, who spent most of his working life at the factory and demonstrated the potter's wheel at the Wedgwood Visitor Centre and in exhibitions for the company worldwide. He threw pots on the wheel for Martha during her Wedgwood factory field trip.

people.name: Pierre Hermé
people.role: French pâtissier dubbed the 'Picasso of Pastry', who led the pastry kitchens of Fauchon and then Ladurée before founding Maison Pierre Hermé Paris in 1998. He demonstrated classic French pastry work — génoise, his signature Carioca chocolate-coffee cake, and quenelles — on this Season 6 episode.

people.name: Madeleine Kamman
people.role: French-born cooking teacher, chef, and author (When French Women Cook; The New Making of a Cook) who directed the School for American Chefs at Beringer Vineyards and hosted PBS's Madeleine Cooks. She joined Martha for an egg-technique episode, making chocolate soufflé among omelets and crème anglaise.

people.name: Bill Gates
people.role: Co-founder and then-CEO of Microsoft, the world's best-known software executive, interviewed by Martha for a technology-themed episode built around sending and receiving email and email etiquette.

people.name: David Macaulay
people.role: British-born American author and illustrator of the bestselling explainer classics The Way Things Work and its 1998 update The New Way Things Work, and winner of the 1991 Caldecott Medal for Black and White. He appeared on the show's Bookshelf segment to present the newly published update.

people.name: Sara Foster
people.role: Chef and cookbook author who cooked for Martha Stewart's Westport catering company after graduating from the New York Restaurant School in 1981, then founded Foster's Market, the Durham, North Carolina gourmet cafe and market, in 1990. She returned to Martha's show to cook Southern dishes including her shrimp and grit cakes.

people.name: Ian Ingersoll
people.role: Ian Ingersoll is a master cabinetmaker whose workshop in West Cornwall, Connecticut — founded in the late 1970s — became nationally known for faithful Shaker chair reproductions after the 1986 Whitney Museum Shaker exhibition. His interlocking-tenon slat-back and rocker designs adapt classic Mount Lebanon Shaker patterns for modern use.

people.name: John D. Williams Jr.
people.role: John D. Williams Jr. served 25 years as the first and only executive director of the National Scrabble Association and was the game's official media spokesman, co-authoring 'Everything Scrabble' with three-time national champion Joe Edley. His 2015 memoir 'Word Nerd' recounts promoting Scrabble on Martha Stewart's show.

people.name: Maurice Sendak
people.role: Maurice Sendak (1928-2012), author-illustrator of 'Where the Wild Things Are' and one of the most celebrated children's-book artists of the 20th century, lived and worked in Ridgefield, Connecticut. He visited Martha's Connecticut television studio in 2000 to discuss his work, the books that shaped him — including 'Mickey Mouse in Pigmy Land' and 'The Prince and the Pauper' — and the importance of reading to children.

people.name: William Cahill
people.role: William P. Cahill is a Galway-born master roof thatcher who completed a five-year apprenticeship in Ireland — training under English master thatcher Peter Brockett and Donegal master Peter Slevin — before emigrating to the U.S., where he thatches roofs nationwide from his base in Ohio. His commissions include the Smithsonian-sponsored rethatching of the historic Jamestown church in Virginia.

people.name: David Moses Bridges
people.role: Passamaquoddy birch bark artist and canoe builder (1962-2017) from Pleasant Point, Maine, who revived traditional Wabanaki birchbark canoe-making, baskets, and winter-bark etching learned from his great-grandfather Sylvester Gabriel. He served on the board of the Abbe Museum in Bar Harbor, was named a Maine Arts Commission Traditional Arts Fellow, and won first prize for traditional basketmaking at the Heard Museum Guild Indian Fair.

people.name: Mrs. Maus
people.role: Nutley, New Jersey neighbor of the young Martha Kostyra who, with her husband, owned a local bakery; Martha grew up helping the couple make their buttery fruitcakes packed with nuts and hand-cut candied fruit, and 'Mrs. Maus's Fruitcake' remained a signature recipe of Martha's Christmas baking repertoire.

people.name: Memrie Lewis
people.role: Landscape designer and one of Martha's closest friends, known for gardens from Charleston to New York to Maine and for Manhattan terrace and rooftop gardens; her namesake layered omelet recipe aired as a Season 5 cooking segment.

people.name: Eve Stone
people.role: Antiques dealer and nationally recognized authority on 16th-19th-century English and Continental copper and brass; founded Eve Stone Antiques, Ltd. in 1970, running it with her daughter Susan from Woodbridge, Connecticut, with earlier shops on Martha's Vineyard and at Manhattan's Place des Antiquaires.

people.name: Eleanora Scarpetta
people.role: Naples-born Italian-American home cook whom Martha heralded as an 'Old World cook'; she was such a hit on Martha Stewart Living that she returned about a dozen times to cook family dishes. Her 2004 cookbook Eleanora's Kitchen (with Sarah Belk King) collects the Italian-American classics viewers saw on the show.

people.name: Bon Yagi
people.role: Japanese-American restaurateur behind New York's T.I.C. Restaurant Group, whose East Village sake bar Decibel (1993) and Sakagura (1997) helped introduce premium sake to American diners. He came on Martha Stewart Living to teach Martha about sake following Decibel's success.

people.name: Sharon Lebewohl
people.role: Daughter of Second Avenue Deli founder Abe Lebewohl and co-author of The 2nd Ave Deli Cookbook (1999), which preserved the recipes of the landmark New York Jewish deli. She shared her family's latke recipe with Martha Stewart Living, published as 'Sharon's Potato Latkes.'

people.name: Necy Guimaraes
people.role: Senior set decorator in Martha Stewart Living Television's art department (c. 1999-2001), listed among the show's Daytime Emmy set-decoration nominees. The tablescapes seen on the program were her professional craft, showcased on air in 'Necy's Tablesetting.'

people.name: Terence Conran
people.role: Sir Terence Conran (1931-2020), British designer, retailer, and restaurateur — founder of Habitat and The Conran Shop and one of the most influential figures in modern home design. In February 2000 he opened Guastavino's, his first American restaurant, in the landmark tile-vaulted Bridgemarket space under Manhattan's Queensboro Bridge, and sat for an interview on Martha Stewart Living that spring.

people.name: Pino Luongo
people.role: Tuscan-born Manhattan restaurateur and cookbook author behind Le Madri, Coco Pazzo, Centolire, and Morso, credited with bringing Tuscan home cooking to New York fine dining in the late 1980s and 1990s. His signature robiola pizza — a split focaccia spread with robiola cheese and finished with white truffle oil, made famous at Le Madri — was published by Martha Stewart Living, and he demonstrated pizza dough on the show in 2000.

places.name: Turkey Hill
places.role: Martha's farmhouse in Westport, Connecticut (1971-2007). Home base for many MSL TV segments — gardens, kitchen, chickens, potting shed.

places.name: Westport, Connecticut
places.role: Westport, CT — site of Turkey Hill, Martha's longtime home.

places.name: Bedford, New York
places.role: Bedford, NY — Cantitoe Corners, Martha's later estate (acquired 2000).

places.name: East Hampton
places.role: East Hampton, NY — Lily Pond Lane house featured in Christmas and summer specials.

places.name: Skylands
places.role: Skylands — Martha's Maine summer house (Edsel Ford's former estate on Mount Desert Island, Seal Harbor).

places.name: Bronson Road
places.role: Bronson Road, Fairfield County, CT — featured in multi-part garden and home segments.

places.name: Murray McMurray Hatchery
places.role: Murray McMurray Hatchery, Webster City, Iowa — world's largest rare-breed poultry hatchery; visited in MSL Season 6.

places.name: Balthazar Bakery
places.role: Balthazar Bakery, NYC — Keith McNally's French bistro and bakery in SoHo.

places.name: Mashantucket Pequot Museum
places.role: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center, CT — Native American history museum.

places.name: Wave Hill
places.role: Wave Hill, Bronx, NY — 28-acre public garden and cultural center overlooking the Hudson.

places.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
places.role: Metropolitan Museum of Art, NYC — featured exhibits (e.g. Vermeer) visited as field trips.

places.name: Bronx Zoo
places.role: Bronx Zoo, NYC — Deck the Zoo segment, Making Vines segment.

places.name: William Doyle Galleries
places.role: William Doyle Galleries, NYC — auction house featured in MSL Season 6.

places.name: Shelburne Museum
places.role: Shelburne Museum, Vermont — folk-art and Americana museum.

places.name: Peckerwood Gardens
places.role: Peckerwood Garden, Hempstead, Texas — designer John Fairey's experimental botanic garden.

places.name: Yucca Do Nursery
places.role: Yucca Do Nursery, Texas — specialty plant nursery linked with Peckerwood Garden.

places.name: Gilberties Herb Farm
places.role: Gilberties Herb Gardens, Easton, CT — organic herb farm.

places.name: White Flower Farm
places.role: White Flower Farm, Litchfield, CT — mail-order nursery.

places.name: Durling's Citrus Farm
places.role: Durling's Citrus Farm — featured in citrus segment.

places.name: Iggy's Bakery
places.role: Iggy's Bread of the World, Cambridge MA — artisan bakery.

places.name: Cupcake Cafe
places.role: Cupcake Cafe, NYC — known for floral buttercream cakes.

places.name: Costello Studio
places.role: Costello Studio — leather-tooling craft segment.

places.name: Dreesen's Donuts
places.role: Dreesen's, East Hampton — famous cake-doughnut maker.

places.name: Glen Horowitz Bookseller
places.role: Glenn Horowitz Bookseller — rare-books dealer (East Hampton/NYC).

places.name: Elias' Corner
places.role: Elias' Corner, Astoria Queens — Greek seafood restaurant; 'Pit Stop' field trip.

places.name: New York Tree Trust
places.role: New York Tree Trust — public-tree stewardship program.

places.name: Marble House
places.role: Marble House, Newport RI — Vanderbilt cottage (Preservation Society).

places.name: Hog Island Oyster Farm
places.role: Hog Island Oyster Co., Tomales Bay California — featured in oyster-farming field trip.

places.name: Center Art Studio
places.role: Center Art Studio, NYC — restoration studio for ceramics, glass, and decorative arts.

places.name: Columbine Ranch
places.role: Columbine Ranch — Western field-trip destination featured in MSL.

places.name: Westminster Dog Show
places.role: Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show, Madison Square Garden NYC — annual field-trip subject.

places.name: Mount Desert Island
places.role: Mount Desert Island, Maine — home to Acadia National Park and Skylands.

places.name: Frances Palmer Pottery
places.role: Frances Palmer Pottery, Weston Connecticut — hand-thrown earthenware studio.

places.name: Guy Wolff Pottery
places.role: Guy Wolff Pottery, Bantam CT — English-style hand-thrown flower pots.

places.name: Jonathan Adler Pottery
places.role: Jonathan Adler's pottery studio (early career segment before the home-goods empire).

places.name: Russian Tea Room
places.role: The Russian Tea Room, 150 W 57th Street NYC — Imperial-Russian café next to Carnegie Hall.

places.name: Best Cellars
places.role: Best Cellars, NYC — wine shop organized by taste profile (Fizzy/Fresh/Soft/Luscious/Big/Sweet) rather than region.

places.name: Nanz Custom Hardware
places.role: Nanz, NYC — custom architectural hardware (door knobs, hinges, latches) for high-end residential and historic restorations.

places.name: Kate Spade
places.role: Kate Spade — handbags and lifestyle brand featured on a Madison Avenue field trip.

places.name: Atlantic Blanket Company
places.role: Atlantic Blanket Company, Maine — wool-blanket maker, three-Bayard-Bedstead segment.

places.name: Wildwood Stables
places.role: Wildwood Stables — equestrian field-trip destination.

places.name: Bard Center
places.role: Bard Graduate Center, NYC — decorative-arts research and exhibitions (E.W. Godwin field trip).

places.name: Seventh Regiment Antiques
places.role: Seventh Regiment Armory Antiques Show, Park Avenue NYC — annual fine-antiques fair.

places.name: Maine Antiques Digest
places.role: Maine Antiques Digest — long-running trade publication for antiques dealers and collectors.

places.name: Balthazar Restaurant
places.role: Balthazar (80 Spring Street, SoHo NYC) — Keith McNally's French brasserie, opened 1997. Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson were co-chefs in the early 2000s. MSL S5 E146V "Balthazar Restaurant: Brandade de Morue, Braised Ribs."

places.name: Frenchette
places.role: Frenchette (TriBeCa NYC) — Riad Nasr & Lee Hanson's own restaurant after Balthazar. Cookbook Frenchette Bistro Cooking (2024).

places.name: Le Bernardin
places.role: Le Bernardin (NYC) — Eric Ripert's three-Michelin-star French seafood restaurant. The Le Bernardin Cookbook (1998).

places.name: Frontera Grill
places.role: Frontera Grill / Topolobampo (Chicago) — Rick Bayless's regional Mexican restaurants.

places.name: Picholine
places.role: Picholine (NYC, opened 1993 by Terrance Brennan; named after the green olive). Mediterranean/French. Closed 2015.

places.name: Union Square Cafe
places.role: Union Square Cafe (NYC) — Danny Meyer's first restaurant (opened 1985). Michael Romano was executive chef from 1988. Their famous Caesar salad featured on MSL TV.

places.name: Watershed
places.role: Watershed (Decatur GA) — Scott Peacock's Southern restaurant. Edna Lewis was the elder co-creator.

places.name: Rosa Mexicano
places.role: Rosa Mexicano (NYC, est. 1984 by Josefina Howard) — first restaurant to elevate Mexican cuisine in NYC. Famous for tableside guacamole and pomegranate margaritas.

places.name: Le Cirque
places.role: Le Cirque (NYC, Sirio Maccioni). Egidiana "Egi" Maccioni is the consulting chef. Osteria del Circo is its Tuscan sibling.

places.name: Daniel
places.role: Daniel (NYC) — Daniel Boulud's flagship French restaurant on East 65th St.

places.name: Russ & Daughters
places.role: Russ & Daughters (179 E Houston St, Lower East Side NYC, est. 1914) — Jewish appetizing store, third-generation under Mark Russ Federman during MSL TV era. Smoked fish, caviar, bagels.

places.name: Eli Wilner & Co.
places.role: Eli Wilner & Company (NYC) — antique-frame restorer and dealer; framed pieces for many of Martha's homes.

places.name: Olives
places.role: Olives (Charlestown MA, later NYC and elsewhere) — Todd English's Mediterranean restaurant. Figs is its sibling pizza concept.

places.name: La Varenne
places.role: École de Cuisine La Varenne — Anne Willan's French cooking school (originally Paris, later Burgundy).

places.name: Beppe
places.role: Beppe (NYC) — Cesare Casella's Tuscan restaurant (opened 2001).

places.name: Parrots of the World
places.role: Parrots of the World (Rockville Centre, NY) — Marc Morrone's pet shop, co-founded 1978 with Nick Guerra. Set of Petkeeping with Marc Morrone (2003–2006); also the source of many MSL TV petkeeping segments.

places.name: Swans Island Company
places.role: Swans Island Company (Northport, Maine, originally Swans Island) — handwoven natural-dyed wool blankets. Featured on MSL TV; sometimes misremembered as "Atlantic Blanket Company".

places.name: Westport, Connecticut
places.role: Westport, Fairfield County, CT — site of Turkey Hill (Martha's home 1971–2007) and base of her catering business that preceded the magazine and TV show.

places.name: Greens Farms
places.role: Greens Farms neighborhood of Westport, CT — where Turkey Hill stood. Pre-1648 settlement; later given its name from the local Green family.

places.name: Katonah / Bedford
places.role: Katonah / Bedford, NY — site of Cantitoe Corners, Martha's 153-acre farm. Formerly Sycamore Farms (settled 1784).

places.name: Seal Harbor, Maine
places.role: Seal Harbor, Mount Desert Island, Maine — site of Skylands, Martha's summer house (built 1923–1925 by architect Duncan Candler for Edsel and Eleanor Ford; landscape by Jens Jensen).

places.name: Cabot Hosiery Mills
places.role: Cabot Hosiery Mills, Northfield VT (founded 1978 by Marc Cabot) — Vermont sock manufacturer; later launched the Darn Tough brand in 2004. During MSL TV era was a B2B private-label maker.

places.name: Brewery Ommegang
places.role: Brewery Ommegang, Cooperstown NY (founded 1997 by Don Feinberg and Wendy Littlefield) — Belgian-style brewery; sold to Duvel Moortgat in 2003.

places.name: Straus Family Creamery
places.role: Straus Family Creamery, Marshall CA (founded 1941, became first certified-organic creamery west of the Mississippi in 1994). Note spelling: "Straus" not "Strauss". MSL TV multi-part field trip.

places.name: Saint Basil Seminary
places.role: Saint Basil Seminary, Stamford CT (founded 1933) — Ukrainian Catholic seminary; home of the Ukrainian Museum + Library that supplied the Ukrainian Easter Bread / Pysanky segment (MSL S6 E305V).

places.name: Vanns Spices
places.role: Vanns Spices, Baltimore MD (founded 1981 by Virginia Limansky and Ann Wilder). Featured on MSL S8 E153V.

places.name: JustUs Frenchies
places.role: JustUs Dogs / JustUs Frenchies (Trappe MD; Suzanne Orban-Stagle + Ronald Readmond) — the French Bulldog breeder where Martha got Francesca and Sharkey.

places.name: Central Pennsylvania Avian Club
places.role: Central Pennsylvania Avian Club (CPAC), Bloomsburg PA (founded 1974) — bird/canary breeders association. Martha was celebrity judge at their 21st Annual Spring Show, May 3–4 1997, with poultry judge Johnny Batson. Episode aired Sept 18 1997 (MSL S5 E10). The mysterious "Avian Club PT.1 / PT.2 / PT.3" segments.

places.name: Hyman Hendler & Sons
places.role: Hyman Hendler & Sons (NYC, founded 1900s) — Garment District ribbon merchant favored by designers and crafters; closed 2014. MSL S4 E20.

places.name: City Bakery
places.role: City Bakery, NYC (founded 1990 by Maury Rubin) — pretzel croissants and the famous hot chocolate festival. MSL S2 E24 field trip.

places.name: Tavern on the Green
places.role: Tavern on the Green, Central Park NYC — Christmas field trip on MSL S3 E15.

places.name: The River Café
places.role: The River Café, DUMBO Brooklyn — under the Brooklyn Bridge on a barge; opened 1977 by Buzzy O'Keeffe. MSL S4 E5.

places.name: New York Botanical Garden
places.role: New York Botanical Garden (Bronx, founded 1891) — Holiday Train Show field trip on MSL S2 E14.

places.name: Mount Vernon
places.role: Mount Vernon, VA — George Washington's plantation and museum. MSL S9 E61 field trip.

places.name: Scott Arboretum
places.role: Scott Arboretum at Swarthmore College, PA — public garden across the college campus. MSL S9 E96.

places.name: Esca
places.role: Esca, NYC (opened 2000; closed 2024) — David Pasternack's Italian seafood restaurant with Mario Batali and Joe Bastianich; known for crudo.

places.name: Citronelle
places.role: Citronelle, Washington DC (opened 1993; closed 2012) — Michel Richard's flagship.

places.name: Matsuhisa
places.role: Matsuhisa, Beverly Hills (opened 1987) — Nobu Matsuhisa's original restaurant before the Nobu chain.

places.name: Lionel Trains
places.role: Lionel LLC — American toy-train manufacturer (founded 1900); MSL TV factory field trip.

places.name: Yale Alley Cats
places.role: Yale Alley Cats — a cappella group from Yale University; repeat MSL TV guests including "Singing with Yale Alley Kats with MS" segments.

places.name: Vermeer Exhibit at Metropolitan Museum of Art
Faux Bois Artist (Carlos Cortez, San Antonio, TX)
Bard Center Tour of EW Godwin
Plant of the Week - Bold Foliage
Urban Archaeology
places.role: Architectural-salvage pioneer founded by Gil Shapiro in SoHo in 1978, when its crews combed New York demolition sites and dumpsters for ornament, lighting, and fixtures; early customers included Andy Warhol. From its TriBeCa flagship the company later evolved into a leading maker of restoration lighting, bath fittings, and artisan tile drawn from its salvage archive — MSL toured the operation in two field-trip segments.

places.name: Puerto Rico
places.role: Caribbean island and U.S. territory that MSL visited for a two-part Season 4 travel special, with stops including the Ron Barrilito rum works in Bayamón and field segments on plantains and bananas.

places.name: Chappellet Winery
places.role: Family-owned winery founded in 1967 by Donn and Molly Chappellet on Pritchard Hill, high above Napa Valley — the valley's second new winery established after the repeal of Prohibition. Its pyramid-shaped winery building, designed with artist Ed Moses, and its pioneering high-elevation hillside Cabernet Sauvignon made Pritchard Hill famous; visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
places.role: 52-acre public garden founded in 1910 beside Prospect Park, renowned for its Cherry Esplanade, Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden, and Magnolia Plaza. MSL filmed tulip and pansy planting there and toured its magnolia collection at peak spring bloom.

places.name: New Orleans
places.role: Louisiana's storied port city on the Mississippi, founded in 1718 and famous for its French Quarter, Creole cooking, and historic garden districts; MSL made two Season 7 field trips there.

places.name: Harvard University
places.role: America's oldest university, founded in 1636 in Cambridge, Massachusetts. MSL visited two of its natural-history treasures: the Ware Collection of Blaschka Glass Flowers — some 4,300 astonishingly lifelike botanical models crafted by Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka between 1887 and 1936 — and a butterfly exhibit on campus.

places.name: Sage Street Antiques
places.role: Weekends-only antiques shop at the corner of Sage and Division Streets in Sag Harbor, N.Y., a cult favorite among Hamptons treasure hunters for its ever-changing, priced-to-sell stock of vintage glass, china, silver, and country furnishings — lines form before opening. Featured in a first-season MSL antiquing segment.

places.name: Bark Frameworks
places.role: Fine-art framing house founded by artist Jared Bark in his SoHo loft in 1969, which grew into one of the country's foremost preservation framers, designing museum-grade frames for major institutions and contemporary artists — later from a Long Island City workshop, employee-owned since 2017. Featured in a first-season MSL framing segment.

places.name: Guthman Antiques
places.role: Connecticut antiques dealership tied to Fairfield County's noted Guthman dealers: Pat Guthman Antiques of Southport specialized in 18th- and early 19th-century hearth-cooking antiques and keeping-room furnishings — copper, brass, pottery, and iron — while William H. Guthman's Guthman Americana in Westport was a nationally known source of Colonial and Federal-period Americana and a longtime Antiques Roadshow appraiser's shop. Featured in a first-season MSL antiques segment.

places.name: Consignmart
places.role: Consignment shop in Westport, Connecticut — Martha's longtime hometown — visited in an early MSL segment on secondhand furnishings.

places.name: Allied Down
places.role: Down-and-feather bedding company featured in a Season 3 segment on down pillows and comforters.

places.name: Boston Turning Works
places.role: Custom architectural wood-turning shop long based in Watertown, Massachusetts, producing balusters, newel posts, porch posts, and a collection of historically accurate finials researched from period models for restoration work. Featured in a Season 3 MSL segment.

places.name: Fischer & Page
places.role: Wholesale florist on West 28th Street in Manhattan's historic Flower District, prized by floral designers for unusual varieties — fritillaria, ranunculus, and tree peonies in season. Visited in a Season 3 MSL flower segment.

places.name: Brooklyn Rose Garden
places.role: Rose garden in Brooklyn, N.Y., visited in a Season 3 MSL gardening segment — most likely the Cranford Rose Garden at Brooklyn Botanic Garden, which opened in 1928 with a gift from subway engineer Walter Cranford and holds one of North America's broadest rose collections, with well over 5,000 plants.

places.name: Disney Institute
places.role: Walt Disney World's hands-on learning resort near Orlando, opened by Michael Eisner in February 1996 and modeled in part on New York's Chautauqua Institution, with more than 80 programs in cooking, gardening, animation, and the arts. Featured on MSL in a Season 4 contest-winner segment. The resort campus closed in 2003 to become Disney's Saratoga Springs Resort, and the name survives as Disney's corporate-training arm.

places.name: Manhattan Fruitier
places.role: New York City purveyor of hand-arranged fresh-fruit gift baskets, founded in 1987 with arrangements inspired by Dutch still-life painting; it grew into a national mail-order business pairing fruit with cheeses, chocolates, and New York artisan foods. Featured in a Season 4 MSL segment.

places.name: Edible Schoolyard
places.role: Chef Alice Waters's pioneering garden-and-kitchen classroom, founded in 1995 at Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School in Berkeley, California, where students grow, cook, and share food from a one-acre organic garden; it became the model for the national Edible Schoolyard Project. Visited in a Season 5 MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Bell'occhio
places.role: San Francisco specialty shop opened in 1988 by Claudia Schwartz at 10 Brady Street — the name is Italian for "beautiful eye" — famed for antique French ribbons, handmade boxes, stationery, and Parisian ephemera sourced from small European ateliers. Visited in a Season 5 MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Strawberry Hill
places.role: Eighteenth-century estate at Irish Town, some 3,000 feet up in Jamaica's Blue Mountains above Kingston, bought in 1972 by Island Records founder Chris Blackwell — Bob Marley recuperated there after his 1976 shooting — and opened in 1994 as the first Caribbean hotel of Blackwell's Island Outpost group, rebuilt in traditional Jamaican Georgian style with hand-carved fretwork. MSL Season 5 segments toured its gardens and fretwork.

places.name: Newfoundland
places.role: Rugged North Atlantic island that, with Labrador, forms Canada's easternmost province — known for its fishing outports, icebergs, and the Norse landing site at L'Anse aux Meadows. Destination of a Season 5 MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Tinsel Trading Company
places.role: Garment District institution born in 1933 when Arch Bergoffen bought a French metallic-thread importer and renamed it, amassing antique tinsel threads, metallic trims, tassels, and vintage millinery flowers; his granddaughter Marcia Ceppos took over the West 37th Street shop in 1989, and Martha featured it repeatedly from the 1990s on. Seen here in a Season 5 ornament-making segment; the shop later relocated to Berkeley, California.

places.name: Jamaica
places.role: Caribbean island nation south of Cuba, third-largest island of the Greater Antilles, visited in a Season 5 MSL field-trip episode — part of a run of Jamaica segments that also toured Strawberry Hill in the Blue Mountains above Kingston.

places.name: Bendheim Glass
places.role: S.A. Bendheim, the family-run specialty architectural glass house founded in Greenwich Village in 1927 by Sem and Margaret Bendheim, is best known for Restoration Glass — mouth-blown window glass made with Germany's Lamberts glassworks whose gentle waviness suits historic buildings, and which has been installed at the White House, Monticello, and Mount Vernon. Toured in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Cycle Path Bikes
places.role: Bicycle shop toured in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Secondhand Rose
places.role: Suzanne Lipschutz's celebrated New York shop, opened on Hudson Street in 1965, grew into the country's premier source of rare vintage wallpaper — tens of thousands of rolls hunted down over five decades for clients ranging from film sets to celebrities, with a major donation of swatches to the Cooper Hewitt design museum in 1991. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Beds & Borders
places.role: Wholesale nursery founded in 1988 by Kathryn Pufahl in Laurel, on Long Island's North Fork, known for sophisticated container plantings and an unusual range of annuals, perennials, and grasses supplied to garden centers and designers across the Northeast. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Nevis
places.role: Small volcanic island in the Caribbean's Leeward chain and the smaller half of the Federation of St. Kitts and Nevis; the birthplace of Alexander Hamilton, it is known for the quiet plantation-inn retreats built into its restored sugar estates. Featured in the MSL travel segment 'Nevis Details'.

places.name: Cutchogue
places.role: Hamlet in the Town of Southold on Long Island's North Fork, settled by English colonists in the 1600s and home to the circa-1649 Old House, a National Historic Landmark on the village green; today it sits amid North Fork farmland and wine country. Site of an MSL barbecue field-trip segment.

places.name: Eve Stone Antiques
places.role: Eve Stone Antiques, Ltd., founded in 1970 in the carriage house of Stone's Martha's Vineyard home and later based in Woodbridge, Connecticut, specializes in 16th–19th-century English and Continental copper and brass — cookware, candlesticks, chandeliers, and fireplace equipment. Stone is a nationally known expert and lecturer in the field. Toured in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Hinckley Yachts
places.role: Storied Maine boatbuilder founded in 1928 in Southwest Harbor on Mount Desert Island, famed for elegant sailing yachts like the fiberglass Bermuda 40 (launched 1960) and, from the mid-1990s, the jet-drive Picnic Boat. Its Southwest Harbor yard was toured in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Fortuny
places.role: Venetian textile house founded by Spanish-born designer Mariano Fortuny y Madrazo, whose Giudecca factory — opened in the early 1920s in a former convent — still hand-prints his richly patterned cotton fabrics using techniques kept secret since his lifetime. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Israel Sack, Inc.
places.role: Manhattan firm built by Lithuanian-born cabinetmaker Israel Sack (1883–1959), who opened his first shop on Boston's Charles Street and became the preeminent dealer in early American antique furniture, supplying collectors such as Henry Ford and Henry Francis du Pont and virtually every major American museum; his sons ran the firm until it closed in 2002. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Steinway & Sons
places.role: Piano maker founded in Manhattan in 1853 by German immigrant Henry E. Steinway, whose Astoria, Queens factory has hand-built its concert grands since the 1870s. The factory was toured in the two-part MSL segment 'The Making of a Steinway Piano'.

places.name: Rao's
places.role: Southern Italian restaurant opened in 1896 on the corner of Pleasant Avenue and East 114th Street in East Harlem — famously the hardest table in New York, its handful of tables informally 'owned' by regulars since the late 1970s. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Sony
places.role: Global electronics and entertainment corporation founded in Tokyo in 1946; one of its facilities was toured in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: New York Public Library
places.role: Landmark research and lending library system founded in 1895, whose Beaux-Arts main branch on Fifth Avenue — opened in 1911 and guarded by the marble lions Patience and Fortitude — is one of New York City's great civic buildings. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Holland
places.role: Holland — the Netherlands — is the heart of the world's flower-bulb industry, famed for its tulip fields, canals, and vast flower markets. Martha toured the country in a two-part travel field trip.

places.name: Fernleigh Topiary Gardens
places.role: Topiary garden toured in a two-part MSL garden-visit segment; the episode guide titles the March 1999 outing "New York Botanical Garden: Fernleigh Topiary Garden," pairing it with a Botanical Garden field trip.

places.name: Vermont
places.role: The Green Mountain State — northern New England's land of dairy farms, covered bridges, fall foliage, and maple syrup, of which it is the nation's leading producer. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Middleton Place
places.role: National Historic Landmark plantation on the Ashley River near Charleston, South Carolina, seat of the Middleton family — including Arthur Middleton, a signer of the Declaration of Independence. Its terraced gardens, begun by Henry Middleton around 1741, are considered the oldest landscaped gardens in the United States. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Old Chatham Sheepherding Company
places.role: Sheep dairy and creamery founded in 1993 by Tom and Nancy Clark in the Columbia County village of Old Chatham, New York; it grew into the largest sheep dairy in the United States, and its Hudson Valley Camembert and sheep's-milk yogurts won national acclaim. Visited in an MSL field-trip segment.

places.name: Habitat for Humanity
places.role: International nonprofit founded in 1976 by Millard and Linda Fuller in Americus, Georgia, that builds simple, affordable houses with volunteer labor and homeowners' own "sweat equity." Featured in an MSL segment on volunteer house construction.

places.name: Little & Lewis
places.role: Garden-art studio and celebrated display garden of sculptors George Little and David Lewis on Bainbridge Island, Washington, begun in 1992 and known for water-inspired cast-concrete botanical sculpture — giant leaves, columns, and fountains — photographed for books and television nationwide. The pair later chronicled the garden in the award-winning A Garden Gallery (2005); on MSL they demonstrated casting concrete hosta leaves.

places.name: Heronswood
places.role: Botanical garden and famed specialty nursery in Kingston, Washington, founded in 1987 by plant explorer Dan Hinkley and architect Robert Jones; its mail-order catalog introduced rare, wild-collected plants to American gardeners before the nursery was sold to Burpee in 2000 (the garden is now run by the Port Gamble S'Klallam Tribe). Toured alongside the Bloedel Reserve's moss garden in an MSL field trip.

places.name: Bloedel Reserve
places.role: Public garden on Bainbridge Island, Washington — the former 140-acre estate of timber executive Prentice Bloedel (MacMillan Bloedel) and his wife Virginia, opened to the public in 1988. Its famed moss garden, laid out by landscape architect Richard Haag in 1982 from roughly 275,000 hand-planted moss plugs, is among the largest in the country; MSL toured it alongside nearby Heronswood in a Puget Sound gardens field trip.

places.name: Atlantic Art
places.role: Almost certainly Atlantic Art Glass, the Maine hot-glass studio and gallery of glass artists Linda and Ken Perrin — founded in the early 1990s in Bar Harbor and relocated to a brick warehouse in downtown Ellsworth in 2005. Perrin's blown glass is held in the permanent collections of the Corning Museum of Glass and Venice's Murano Glass Museum; MSL taped a glassblowing demonstration at the studio during its Bar Harbor years.

places.name: Mikimoto
places.role: Japanese pearl house founded in 1893 in Toba by Kokichi Mikimoto, who produced the world's first cultured pearl that year and by 1913 had opened stores from London to New York; production centered on the island near Toba now known as Mikimoto Pearl Island. MSL's two-part segment followed the company's pearl-cultivation process.

places.name: Arthur Avenue
places.role: Main street of the Belmont section of the Bronx — New York's 'real Little Italy', settled by Italian immigrants around the turn of the twentieth century. Its centerpiece, the Arthur Avenue Retail Market, opened in 1940 when Mayor Fiorello La Guardia moved the neighborhood's pushcart vendors indoors; MSL went shopping among its Italian butchers, bakers, and delis.

places.name: College of the Atlantic
places.role: Small college on Frenchman Bay in Bar Harbor, Maine, founded in 1969, where every student pursues a single self-designed major: human ecology. It operates offshore research stations including the Alice Eno Field Research Station on Great Duck Island, and was featured during MSL's Mount Desert Island-area Maine coverage.

places.name: Great Duck Island
places.role: Island south of Mount Desert Island, Maine, supporting some of the largest breeding colonies of Leach's storm-petrels and black guillemots in the lower 48, plus a historic lighthouse. College of the Atlantic students summer there studying seabirds at the college's field research station (named for trustee Alice Eno in 2000); MSL's 'Island Life' segment visited the island.

places.name: Acadia National Park
places.role: The first national park east of the Mississippi — established as Lafayette National Park in 1919 and renamed Acadia in 1929 — covering much of Mount Desert Island, Maine, with its Rockefeller-built carriage roads and Cadillac Mountain, the highest point on the U.S. Atlantic coast. The park sits minutes from Martha's Skylands estate in Seal Harbor, and MSL's Maine-summer episodes made it a natural field-trip destination.

places.name: Iowa State Fair
places.role: Iowa's annual August fair, first held in 1854 and settled on its permanent Des Moines fairgrounds in 1886 — one of the largest state fairs in the country, famous for its life-size butter-cow sculpture, its livestock and food competitions, and for inspiring the novel and musical 'State Fair'. MSL made it a classic late-summer field trip.

places.name: Horton Brasses
places.role: Cromwell, Connecticut manufacturer of reproduction antique furniture and cabinet hardware, founded in 1936 by tool-and-die maker Frank Horton and run by his family for generations. Its more than 1,000 brass pieces are made from dies and patterns taken off actual antique hardware, making it a longtime favorite of period furniture makers and restorers — the craft MSL's segment showcased.

places.name: Charles H. Baldwin & Sons
places.role: West Stockbridge, Massachusetts extract maker founded in 1888, operating out of the same storefront since 1912. Its signature pure vanilla extract is still blended from Madagascar bourbon vanilla beans in a decades-old copper still and aged in oak barrels — the old-fashioned process MSL's vanilla segment featured.

places.name: Estiatorio Milos
places.role: Manhattan outpost of restaurateur Costas Spiliadis's Greek seafood restaurant — the original opened in Montreal in 1979, with the West 55th Street location following in 1997 — renowned for its market-style display of whole Mediterranean fish on ice from which diners choose their meal. MSL's fresh-fish field trip toured the display shortly after the New York opening.

places.name: Radio City Music Hall
places.role: Landmark Art Deco theater at Rockefeller Center, opened December 27, 1932, with interiors by Donald Deskey — the self-styled "Showplace of the Nation" and home of the Rockettes. MSL's two-part backstage tour came on the heels of the theater's celebrated 1999 top-to-bottom restoration.

places.name: Thistle Hill Weavers
places.role: Custom weaving mill founded by textile historian Rabbit Goody in 1989 in an old feed mill near Cherry Valley, New York, specializing in historically accurate reproduction fabrics, carpet, and trim for museums, designers, and Hollywood — its textiles have appeared in more than 70 films and television productions. Goody, formerly curator of textiles at the Farmers' Museum in Cooperstown, demonstrated the mill's work on MSL.

places.name: New York Chinese Scholar's Garden
places.role: Authentic Ming-style scholar's garden at the Staten Island Botanical Garden, Snug Harbor Cultural Center, opened in June 1999 after a team of 40 artisans from Suzhou, China assembled its pavilions, rockeries, and courtyards on site. MSL visited not long after the garden's debut.

places.name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
places.role: 83-acre tropical botanic garden in Coral Gables, Florida, established in 1938 and named for plant explorer David Fairchild; renowned for its palm and cycad collections. One of three stops on MSL's Miami-area field trip, alongside Kerry's Nursery and Joe's Stone Crab.

places.name: Joe's Stone Crab
places.role: Miami Beach institution founded by Joseph Weiss in 1913, credited with popularizing the stone crab; its seasonal claws with mustard sauce made it one of the highest-grossing restaurants in America. Visited on MSL's Florida field trip.

places.name: Belgo
places.role: Belgian mussels-and-frites restaurant group founded in London in 1992 by Denis Blais and André Plisnier, known for its cavernous beer-hall design, monk-robed waiters, and vast list of Belgian beers. Its Manhattan outpost, Belgo Nieuw York at 415 Lafayette Street, supplied MSL's marinière mussel-pot segment.

places.name: Guastavino's
places.role: Restaurant and event space opened by British design impresario Sir Terence Conran on Valentine's Day 2000 beneath the Queensboro Bridge, in the landmark Bridgemarket space whose soaring tiled vaults were built by Rafael Guastavino's firm. MSL's lemon tart segment caught it in its early days as Conran's splashy New York venture.

places.name: American Museum of Natural History
places.role: Founded in 1869, the vast natural history museum on Central Park West is one of the largest in the world. MSL made a field trip through its halls and returned for the Butterfly Conservatory, the live-butterfly vivarium the museum has mounted annually since 1998.

places.name: Doughnut Plant
places.role: Lower East Side bakery started by Mark Isreal in 1994, baking doughnuts from his grandfather Herman's recipe in a tenement basement and delivering them by bicycle to gourmet shops; its first storefront opened on the Lower East Side in 2000. Its all-natural, inventive doughnuts — credited with launching New York's artisanal-doughnut wave — were featured on MSL.

places.name: Scharffen Berger Chocolate Maker
places.role: Artisan chocolate company founded in 1996 in the San Francisco Bay Area by winemaker John Scharffenberger and physician Robert Steinberg — the first new American bean-to-bar chocolate maker in some 50 years and a pioneer of cacao-percentage labeling, later famous for its Berkeley factory. Acquired by Hershey in 2005; its chocolate-making process was featured on MSL.

places.name: Skarstad Violins
places.role: Violin-making and restoration shop of luthier Brian Skarstad, crafting instruments in Pleasantville, New York since 1979. Skarstad, who trained with Peter Prier in Salt Lake City, models his violins and violas on classic Italian examples and has sold instruments to New York Philharmonic players; MSL paid his workshop a field-trip visit.

places.name: The Newtown Bee
places.role: Weekly newspaper of Newtown, Connecticut, published since 1877 and run by the Smith family since 1880. Its companion publication Antiques and the Arts Weekly, spun off from the paper's antiques pages in 1969, made "The Bee" a national authority on the antiques trade — the angle MSL picked up in its segment.

places.name: Hershey Chocolate Factory
places.role: The original Hershey's plant on East Chocolate Avenue in Hershey, Pennsylvania, built by Milton S. Hershey between 1903 and 1905 — for decades the largest chocolate factory in the world and the heart of the company town that grew up around it (production there ceased in 2012). MSL toured the factory in a Season 7 field trip.

places.name: Corky's Ribs & BBQ
places.role: Memphis barbecue institution founded in 1984 by Don Pelts on Poplar Avenue in East Memphis, famous for hickory-smoked pork ribs and repeatedly voted the city's #1 BBQ joint. An early pioneer of overnight rib shipping (from 1987), it later franchised across the South — featured in MSL's Memphis barbecue segment.

places.name: Eastfield Village
places.role: Village of 28 condemned or abandoned 18th- and 19th-century buildings — a 1793 tavern, 1836 church, and 1811 general store among them — dismantled board-by-board, moved, and reassembled by self-taught craftsman Don Carpentier on his family's farmland in East Nassau, NY, beginning in 1971. Home of the Historic Eastfield Foundation's workshops, the longest-running school of historic trades in the country; toured in a multi-part MSL segment.

places.name: Kelmscott Rare Breeds Foundation
places.role: Nonprofit conservation farm founded by Robyn Metcalfe on 150 acres in Lincolnville, Maine (farm established 1993, foundation incorporated 1994), keeping some 200 animals across twenty varieties of rare and endangered sheep, pigs, cattle, horses, and poultry. Instrumental in reestablishing Gloucestershire Old Spots pigs in North America; visited in an MSL farm segment with Marc Morrone.

places.name: Huber Embroideries
places.role: Embroidery atelier featured in an MSL segment on fine embroidery work.

places.name: Noche Flamenca
places.role: Touring flamenco company formed in New York in 1993 by director Martín Santangelo and his wife, Bessie Award-winning dancer Soledad Barrio, dedicated to keeping alive the authentic form of flamenco. Known for regular New York seasons at the Joyce Theater and Lincoln Center; featured in an MSL performance segment.

places.name: Alaska
places.role: The 49th U.S. state (statehood 1959) and by far the largest, purchased from Russia in 1867 — known for its salmon fisheries, glaciers, and Inside Passage ports. Destination of MSL's Alaska-and-Yukon field trip.

places.name: Yukon
places.role: Canadian territory in the country's northwest corner, bordering Alaska, with its capital at Whitehorse; famed as the setting of the Klondike Gold Rush of 1896–99. Visited in MSL's Alaska-and-Yukon field trip.

places.name: Pacific Bell Park
places.role: Waterfront ballpark of the San Francisco Giants at China Basin, opened in April 2000 as the first privately financed major-league park in decades; later renamed SBC Park, then AT&T Park, and today Oracle Park. Visited in an MSL field segment shortly after it opened.

places.name: Schrader Garden
places.role: Private garden toured in an MSL garden-visit segment — likely the Mattituck, Long Island garden of horticulturist Dennis Schrader and Bill Smith, co-founders of the tropical-plant nursery Landcraft Environments (est. 1992). Schrader appeared on Martha Stewart Living TV, and the garden later became the nonprofit Landcraft Garden Foundation, with Martha on its advisory board.

places.name: EthnicGrocer.com
places.role: Chicago dot-com founded in 1999 by Kellogg MBA Parry Singh with co-founder Subhash Bedi, selling hard-to-find international grocery ingredients online through country-specific storefronts (Namaste.com, QueRico.com, gongshee.com). Backed by roughly $47 million from marquee investors including Benchmark and Kleiner Perkins at the height of the e-commerce boom; featured in an MSL segment of the same era.

places.name: Salem Organics
places.role: Salem Organic Soils, the New York company (founded 1986) behind Sweet Peet, a patented organic mulch made by composting shavings-based horse manure with plant tannins into a fine coffee-colored soil dressing. Featured on MSL and used by the gardeners on Martha's own property.

places.name: Old Town Canoe Company
places.role: America's most storied canoe maker, building wood-and-canvas canoes in Old Town, Maine since 1898 on designs inspired by Penobscot birchbark craft. By the late 1920s it was the largest canoe manufacturer in the country, ultimately producing more than 200,000 wood-and-canvas boats; its canoes and workshop were featured in an MSL segment.

places.name: Taku Smokeries
places.role: Smokehouse and seafood processor founded in the early 1980s by Italian-born, Berkeley-trained marine biologist Sandro Lane on the Juneau, Alaska waterfront, producing hot- and cold-smoked wild Alaska salmon shipped nationwide. Visited in an MSL segment.

places.name: Wölffer Estate Vineyard
places.role: Winery founded in 1988 by Hamburg-born entrepreneur Christian Wölffer (originally as Sagpond Vineyards) in Sagaponack on Long Island's South Fork, with a 55-acre sustainably farmed vineyard whose rosé — first released in 1993 — helped define Hamptons wine culture. Visited in an MSL segment.

places.name: Longwood Gardens
places.role: One of America's premier botanical gardens, on the former Pierre S. du Pont estate in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania — du Pont bought the property in 1906 to save its historic trees and completed its famed four-acre Conservatory in 1921. Its annual "A Longwood Christmas" display of lights, trees, and conservatory plantings drew MSL's cameras for a holiday visit.

places.name: Mentoring USA
places.role: One-to-one youth-mentoring nonprofit founded in 1995 by Matilda Raffa Cuomo, former First Lady of New York, as the national successor to the New York State Mentoring Program she began in 1984; it pairs volunteer mentors with children ages 7–21. Featured in an MSL community-service segment.

places.name: Mount Auburn Cemetery
places.role: Consecrated in 1831 in Cambridge and Watertown, Massachusetts, America's first landscaped rural "garden" cemetery — a model that helped inspire the nation's public-parks movement. Its 175 acres of horticulture and monuments hold Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, Winslow Homer, and Mary Baker Eddy, and drew an MSL visit.

places.name: Sotheby's Restoration
places.role: The furniture-conservation arm of the Sotheby's auction house, founded in the late 1970s by John Stair, whose team of master cabinetmakers, gilders, polishers, and lacquer specialists restored fine antique furniture in New York City and, from the mid-1980s, Claverack, New York; it was later acquired by Stair's son Colin and renamed Stair Restoration. MSL toured the workshop in a factory-visit segment.

places.name: Hoyt & Bond
places.role: Children's clothing label and shop founded by former documentary filmmaker Elizabeth Beer, named for two neighboring Brooklyn streets, with a storefront opened in 1998 at 246 Smith Street; it was known for hand-knit woolens and washable cotton-velvet pieces in unusually rich colors, later adding adult sizes by parental demand. Featured in an MSL segment on children's clothing.

places.name: Necco
places.role: The New England Confectionery Company, formed in a 1901 Boston-area merger with roots in Oliver Chase's 1847 lozenge-cutting machine — long billed as the oldest continuously operating candy company in the United States, and maker of Necco Wafers and Sweethearts conversation hearts. MSL toured its longtime Cambridge, Massachusetts factory in a field-trip segment.

places.name: Pier Antiques Show
